themes_detail.label: Graffiti outbreak this week
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked dramatically to 30 this week versus a baseline of 1.8 complaints per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1,614% increase (z-score: 8.85)—suggesting either a coordinated tagging campaign or sudden deterioration in enforcement/cleanup response in Morris Park/Pelham Parkway.
evidence: 30 graffiti complaints filed this week vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 8.85 indicates statistically extreme outlier event
1,614% spike represents most severe deviation across all complaint categories
reporting_angles: Map this week's graffiti complaints to identify geographic hotspots and interview affected residents/business owners
Contact NYPD and Sanitation Department to determine if crews are stretched thin or if organized tagging crews are active in the district

themes_detail.label: Water system failures two weeks ago
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints jumped to 63 two weeks ago against an 8-week baseline of 16.1 per week—a 291% spike (z-score: 5.3)—potentially indicating a DEP infrastructure failure or burst mains affecting multiple buildings in the district.
evidence: 63 water system complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 16.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.3 indicates highly significant statistical anomaly
Converges with repeated CB budget requests for DEP capital funding and catch basin cleaning
reporting_angles: Request DEP incident reports and maintenance logs from 2 weeks ago to identify specific street segments affected by water main breaks or flooding
Interview residents in affected buildings about duration of service interruption and property damage; check for filed insurance claims

themes_detail.label: Drug activity spike two weeks ago
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints spiked to 16 two weeks ago from a baseline of 2.0 per week over 8 weeks—a 700% increase (z-score: 6.42)—signaling a potential open-air drug market emergence or trafficking hotspot in the district.
evidence: 16 drug activity complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.42 represents second-highest statistical severity after graffiti spike
No recent Council constituent escalation data available, but timing suggests potential emergence rather than long-standing issue
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaint locations with NYPD crime data and precinct activity reports to identify specific corners or parks becoming drug markets
Interview community residents, merchants, and local precinct about enforcement response and any visible trafficking activity

themes_detail.label: Overgrown tree branches this week
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints jumped to 7 this week from a baseline of 1.4 per week—a 409% increase (z-score: 4.62)—indicating potential hazards on streets or compromised sightlines that could pose traffic and pedestrian safety risks.
evidence: 7 overgrown tree complaints filed this week vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.62 indicates statistically significant spike
Aligns with CB budget requests for park reconstructions and Department of Parks maintenance
reporting_angles: Map this week's complaints to verify if concentrated in parks or street rights-of-way; photograph hazards
Contact Parks Department and local Parks Enforcement Patrol to determine if there is a pruning schedule backlog or staffing shortage

themes_detail.label: Rodent complaints two weeks ago
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints rose to 12 two weeks ago from an 8-week baseline of 4.1 per week—a 191% increase (z-score: 4.47)—reflecting potential sanitation or structural issues in residential buildings, consistent with district's repeated animal pest control budget requests.
evidence: 12 rodent complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 4.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.47 represents significant statistical outlier
Mirrors CB's consistent budget requests for animal and pest control to Department of Health; suggests chronic infestation problem
reporting_angles: Examine whether complaints cluster in NYCHA buildings or private housing; request DOH inspection records and violation data
Interview residents about building conditions (sealed gaps, trash management) and whether exterminator access was denied or delayed
